tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

dgbr-model-definition: Definition 1, p.2: the paper states the DGBR model operations (CSS initialization, H on all qubits, CNOT, Pauli strings, computational-basis measurement, adaptive use of outcomes). The value matches the passage.
kd-group-definition: Section 'The Z2^n-Kirkwood-Dirac distribution', p.3: the paper states G = Z2^n, basis A (Z eigenstates), basis B built from characters (Eq. 4), Q = Tr(B rho) (Eq. 5) and the phase-point operators (Eq. 6). Its own construction.
thm1-dgbr-connection: Theorem 1.1, p.3; Lemma 3 (S2) and Lemma 4 (S10), Supp. Note II: stated without extra conditions and proved in full. The proof uses real matrix elements of B and the symmetric/antisymmetric split of Re/Im rho, as the value says.
two-qubit-bound-magic-family: Eqs. (16)-(17), p.4; Supp. Note VI: explicit F and rho_lambda. KD-positivity (S31), minimal eigenvalue -1-2sqrt2, facet inequality and Tr(F rho)>1 for lambda>1/20 are stated analytically and cross-checked numerically in Note VII (lambda_magic=0.050, lambda_SD=0.065). I recomputed F's eigenvalues, Tr F=0, Tr F^2=20 and the KD distribution of rho_lambda; all agree. Some intermediate steps are stated, not displayed.
kd-positive-range-and-psd: Supp. Note VI, Eq. (S31)-(S33): the KD distribution is given and read off as nonnegative for lambda in [-1/12, 1/12]. PSD follows from mu_j = lambda nu_j + 1/4 with min eigenvalue of F = -1-2sqrt2. I recomputed both numerically; they agree. The min eigenvalue is stated as 'calculated by standard methods'.
kd-mana-definition: Eq. (18), p.5: M(rho) = log sum |Q| is defined by the paper, with free states (CSS mixtures) and free operations (DGBR model) fixed in the same paragraph.
scope-limits-and-next-step: Introduction p.1 and Discussion p.5: the authors state that the model sits inside Gottesman-Knill and becomes universal with distillable-magic states, that the KD distribution is one instance of a broader class, and name the Park et al. combination as a next step. Stated scope of the authors' own work.
tudor-qrng-device-principle: Section 2.1, p.3: the paper states the device principle (arrival times of single photons in shaped temporal modes, Fig. 1) and that the device is presented in Ref. [22]. Its own device description.
tudor-qrng-dataset-32bit: Section 2.2, p.3: 2.07732758e8 random integers in [0, 4.294967288e9], written on 32 bits. Its own test-data setup.
tudor-randomness-test-setup: Section 2.2, p.4: NIST and Dieharder tests applied to the QRNs, with -Y 1 (resolve ambiguity mode) to repeat 'weak' results. Its own protocol.
tudor-table1-sample-sizes: Table 1, p.5: data sizes 830.9, 1050, 104.9, 125, 100, 100 MB and sample sizes 2.077, 2.621, 0.262, 0.3125, 0.25, 0.25 (x10^8) for QuEST, ANU 1, ANU 2, IDQ web, IDQ Quantis 1 and 2; all Uniform. Matches the value. The ANU and IDQ samples are third-party data the paper compares against.
tudor-fbm-definition: Section 3.1, Eq. (1): the paper defines fBM with H in (0,1) as a zero-mean Gaussian process with covariance (1/2)(t^2H + s^2H - |t-s|^2H). Matches the value.
tudor-fbm-simulation-methods: Section 3.2, p.9-10: Davies-Harte (from [11], detailed in [12] Sec. 2.1.3) and the hybrid scheme of [5] with the Molchan-Golosov kernel were implemented, and the QRN versus PRN paths use the hybrid scheme. Its own computational setup.
tudor-fbm-test-routines: Section 3.2, p.10: Eqs. (4)-(6) and the text list the mean, variance, chi-square test for fractional Gaussian noise and the 2D correlation structure as the implemented test routines.
tudor-fbm-error-metrics-definition: Section 3.2, Eqs. (7)-(9), p.10: epsilon 1, 2, 3 are defined as RMS errors for the mean, the variance against t^2H, and the covariance against gamma(t_k,t_j). The text states they are RMSEs for the first two moments and the covariance. The square roots are lost in the text layer.
tudor-rfsv-model-definition: Section 4.1, Eq. (10), p.14: the model sigma_t = sigma_0 exp(X_t) with the fOU-type dX_t is stated as 'the following model from [14]', with the parameter conditions. The remark that the fOU choice ensures stationarity is a statement of the authors, not shown here.
tudor-fsabr-model-definition: Section 4.2, Eqs. (12)-(13), p.17: dS/S = alpha_t (rho dB + rho-bar dW), alpha_t = alpha_0 exp(nu B^H_t), with B and W independent and B^H the fBM driven by B; rho-bar = sqrt(1-rho^2), the root lost in the text layer. Matches the value.
tudor-tvo-payoff-definitions: Section 4.3, Eqs. (16)-(18), p.19-20: the TV call, the (preassigned) target level sigma, the scaling note, and the TV put with sigma in the denominator, called a new contract type. Matches the value.
scope-review-critical-assessment: Abstract, p.1 and Section 1, p.2: the paper states it reviews tensor networks in ML and gives a critical assessment of the state of the art, advantages and challenges. Its own scope.
two-approaches-native-and-compression: Section 1, p.2: the paper frames the field as two approaches, TNs as direct learning architectures (MPS, TTN, PEPS) and TNs as structured compression of NNs, and organizes the review around them. Settled as the paper's own framing; it is not a proof that these are the only two ways.
terminology-order-dimension-shape: Section 2, p.3: 'we use the word order to denote ..., dimension for ..., and shape for ...'. The paper defines its own terms.
gauge-freedom-definition: Section 2.3, p.6: the paper describes gauge freedom as inserting an invertible matrix and its inverse between nodes, leaving the global tensor unchanged and giving infinitely many equivalent local tensors. This is its own account of the term; the underlying fact is cited to Biamonte and Bergholm (2017).
methods-openalex-181-articles: Appendix A, p.27: the OpenAlex query initially yielded 1 071 articles, and after removing duplicates, irrelevant items and items not in high-quality venues the dataset has 181 articles. The paper's own dataset construction.
wang2024-data-scope: Section 3 and Table 1, p.4: seven indices (VTHR, ^N225, UKX.L, ^NYA, ^IXIC, ^HSI, MME=F), weekday daily closing prices May 2023 to September 2023, from Yahoo Finance. Stated as the paper says. Caveat for the coordinator: that date range holds about 110 weekdays, which does not fit the 500 + 100 days of Section 3 (p.6); the paper is internally inconsistent here.
wang2024-train-test-split: Section 3, p.6: 500 days training and 100 days testing per index; each day's input is the previous day's closing price and the seven features. Stated as written. Same date-range inconsistency as in the data-scope item.
wang2024-features: Section 3 and Table 2, p.5-6: seven features, four macroeconomic (VIX, EFFR, UMCSENT, DXYNYB) and three technical (MACD, ATR, RSI), chosen for high correlation with the closing price per [37]. The correlation claim is cited, but the feature set is the paper's own setup.
wang2024-correlation-weights: Section 3 p.6 and Section 3.1 Eq. (3), p.8: the bottom row of the correlation weight matrix is added as extra input weights Wcor, and the update rule includes Wcor as an element-wise factor. The paper's own construction.
wang2024-nrmse-definition: Section 3.1 Eq. (2), p.6-7: NRMSE between the true series y and prediction on the testing set, normalized by the sum of (y_i - y-bar)^2, with y-bar the mean of the true series. The equation is partly garbled in the text layer; the value states only what the text says.
wang2024-er-definition: Section 4 Eq. (4), p.10: ER = 1 - NRMSE_RC / NRMSE_ML against the best ML model, and 'near 100% ER indicates negligible relative error achieved by RC'. The paper's own metric.
wang2024-ml-baselines: Section 2.1 p.4 and Section 3.2 p.9: LSTM plus nine regression methods (Lasso, ElasticNet, RandomForestRegressor, LinearRegression, Ridge, SGDRegressor, KNeighborsRegressor, DecisionTreeRegressor, BayesianRidge); cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning select the lowest-error ML model per benchmark. Matches the value.
wang2024-multistep-lstm-adjust: Section 3.2, p.9: multi-step data preparation follows the optical RC approach, regression methods stay as in one-step prediction, LSTM model dimensions are adjusted to the prediction horizon. Matches the value.
wang2024-optical-hardware: Section 3.1, Fig. 3, p.7: continuous-wave 775 nm laser diode, beam waist 1 mm after collimation, 10x beam expander to match the SLM, camera in the time-Fourier domain. Matches the value.
wang2024-slm-input-mapping: Section 3.1, Fig. 4, p.7-8: SLM of 400 x 400 pixels, inputs repeated and stacked to fill the modulation areas (20 x 20 pixel blocks), scaled by beta and a random input weight, camera state rescaled by alpha, sum rescaled to the 0 to 2 pi phase range. Matches the value.
wang2024-optical-nonlinearity: Section 3.1, p.8: the paper states the system's nonlinearity comes from the camera intensity reading and the intensity saturation rate. It is a description of its own apparatus; no test of this attribution is given.
wang2024-multistep-encoding: Section 3.1, p.8-9: 4-step and 10-step examples; for 4-step the input u(t) has 32 values (one closing price and 7 features per step, 4 steps) and the horizon is 4 days of closing prices. Matches the value.

theory_low.kd-informationally-complete-rebit: p.3: informational completeness is cited to Ref. [28], not shown. 'Rebit iff Q real' is a one-line remark that uses it, with no proof. A cited result plus an informal remark.
theory_low.dgbr-positive-equals-kd-positive: p.4: the direction 'rebit DGBR-positive implies KD-positive' follows from Theorem 1.1. The direction 'KD-positive implies rebit' needs Q real to force rho real, which rests on informational completeness cited to Ref. [28] (p.3). No separate proof of the equivalence is given. The paper proves Theorem 1.1 only.
theory_low.thm1-hudson: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 1.2, p.3; proof Lemma 5, Supp. Note III, p.11: the proof starts 'In [31], it was shown that ... |psi> is KD positive if and only if it is of the form' P_{g,chi}|H> (Eq. S11), a cited result used as the first step. Only the CSS identification is proved here. The same group graded Theorem 1.3 LOW for its cited Pauli relation.
theory_low.thm1-covariance: Theorem 1.3, p.3; Lemma 6, Supp. Note IV: the Hadamard and CNOT relations (S17, S18) are proved by direct evaluation. The Pauli-string relation (S16) is only cited to Eq. (29) of Ref. [31]. So the theorem as stated is not wholly proved in this paper. The value says so itself.
theory_low.thm1-products: Theorem 1.4, p.3-4: stated, with 'follows from direct calculation' and no calculation shown in the main text or Supp. Notes. The statement is stated but the proof is absent.
theory_low.kd-positive-simulable: p.4: the first half follows from Theorem 1.1. 'DGBR-positive inputs are efficiently simulable' is a cited result from Ref. [8] (p.3-4). Theorem 8 in Supp. Note V proves correctness only if one can sample efficiently from Q, a condition the value drops.
theory_low.algorithm1-linear-time-correct: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Algorithm 1, Lemma 7 and Theorem 8, Supp. Note V, pp.13-14: Lemma 7 and the Pauli step of Theorem 8's induction both use the covariance relation (S16), which Theorem 1.3 takes from Eq. (29) of Ref. [31] (cited, graded LOW in this group); the H and CNOT steps are 'similar arguments apply', and linear time is asserted.
theory_low.single-qubit-no-bound-magic: p.4: the single-qubit KD-positive set is cited to Theorem 1.1.i of Ref. [29]. The conclusion about bound magic is an inference from that cited result. Not proved in this paper.
theory_low.bound-magic-all-n-ge-2: p.4: a short argument by contradiction. It rests on the product rule (Theorem 1.4, shown only as 'direct calculation') and on the partial-trace property of stabilizer mixtures, which is cited to Ref. [70]. It is an in-text argument, not a stated-and-proved theorem. Note the text says 'every number > 2', while n=2 is the base case.
theory_low.thm2-kd-mana-properties: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 2, p.5; Lemmas 9-11, Supp. Note IX, pp.16-17: additivity (Lemma 10, Eq. S39) uses Theorem 1.4, which the paper states as following 'from direct calculation' with no proof shown (graded LOW in this group), and unitary invariance (Lemma 11) uses Theorem 1.3, whose Pauli relation (S16) is cited to Ref. [31] (graded LOW in this group).
theory_low.corollary1-copies-bound: Corollary 1, p.5: stated with no proof anywhere in the main text or Supp. Notes I-IX. The statement and conditions are present, but the paper does not prove it.
theory_low.tudor-fbm-characterization: Section 3.1: 'It can be shown that...' with no proof and no citation in the paper. A field fact asserted without proof.
theory_low.tudor-fbm-holder-continuity: Section 3.1: 'From (1) we deduce' and Holder continuity are stated with no derivation. The displayed E|W_t-W_s| = |t-s|^2H also looks wrong, since |t-s|^2H is the second moment E[|W_t-W_s|^2], not the first absolute moment. An unproved and apparently misstated claim.
theory_low.tudor-continuous-realized-variance-claim: Section 4.1.2, p.16: 'it can be proved that' the continuous realized variance is the time average of sigma_t^2, with no proof and no citation. A field statement.
theory_low.tensorization-without-truncation-no-savi: Section 2.2, p.4: introduced as 'it is not difficult to see', after a worked reshaping and SVD example. It is an informal argument. No theorem or proof is stated. The Fig. 3 counts are illustrative.
theory_low.edge-contraction-can-increase-memory: Section 2.2, p.5: an informal remark, with the size reasoning in one sentence (index n small relative to the free indices m, p). No theorem or proof.
theory_low.mps-parameter-count-and-inner-product-co: Section 2.4.1, p.7: the 'approximately N d chi^2' count and O(N chi^3 d) scalar-product cost are stated without derivation. These are textbook MPS results given by the authors, not proved here.
theory_low.mpo-costs: Section 2.4.2, p.8 (Fig. 6 caption): O(N d^2 chi^2) parameters and O(N chi^6 d) MPO-on-MPS cost are stated without derivation. Not proved in this paper.
